one_idea.line: Yes. The auditor opening old pages and finding money or a skeleton carries both cuts. The six F1 beats keep his own slam words on the words he says, in one band above his head; moving it 30 px up changes position only. fell (P1) still counts the bill down from 195,000 to 33,000 on 'fell' with the caveat kept. Real pages stay held still, and the sofa and closet plates still carry money and skeleton.

no_invented_numbers.line: No invented figure. k_billed and k_after show only the bill-billed and bill-after rows (195,000 and 33,000) with their producer line 'Tom's Hardware, 29 Oct 2025 (the family's account)', and chip_caveat stays on fell. No slam word or tape has a digit. The figures on th_head, l_lede and l_krafton are printed on their own pages. The placement change touches no figure.

findings.text: On a fresh render, check a frame of each F1 beat: his whole head below the band, captions under his chin, not on his face.
The underline maps to about (307,417)-(772,414); check it crosses the digits.
